statement: The kernel (null space) of an $m \times n$ matrix $A$, defined as $\operatorname{Null}(A) = \{\mathbf{v} \in K^n \mid A\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{0}\}$, has a basis given by the columns of $C$ corresponding to the zero columns of $B$, where $\begin{bmatrix} B \\ C \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} A \\ I \end{bmatrix} P$ is obtained by reducing $\begin{bmatrix} A \\ I \end{bmatrix}$ via column operations (Gaussian elimination) until $B$ is in column echelon form.

symbols.meaning: matrix whose kernel is to be computed
invertible matrix representing the column operations
upper block matrix in column echelon form ($B = AP$)
lower block matrix accumulating column operations ($C = IP = P$)

steps.text: Construct the row-augmented matrix $\begin{bmatrix} A \\ I \end{bmatrix}$ where $I$ is the $n \times n$ identity matrix, and apply column operations via Gaussian elimination to reduce $A$ to a matrix $B$ in column echelon form: $\begin{bmatrix} A \\ I \end{bmatrix} P = \begin{bmatrix} B \\ C \end{bmatrix}$ for an invertible matrix $P$.
Multiply blockwise to obtain the relations $AP = B$ and $IP = C = P$, which directly implies $AC = B$.

Relate membership in the kernel to $B$: a vector $\mathbf{v}$ satisfies $A\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{0}$ if and only if $B\mathbf{w} = \mathbf{0}$, where $\mathbf{w} = P^{-1}\mathbf{v} = C^{-1}\mathbf{v}$ (or equivalently, $\mathbf{v} = C\mathbf{w}$).
Since $B$ is in column echelon form, $B\mathbf{w} = \mathbf{0}$ holds if and only if the nonzero entries of $\mathbf{w}$ correspond exclusively to the zero columns of $B$.

Multiplying by $C$ yields $\mathbf{v} = C\mathbf{w}$, demonstrating that $\mathbf{v} \in \operatorname{Null}(A)$ if and only if $\mathbf{v}$ is a linear combination of the columns of $C$ corresponding to the zero columns of $B$, which therefore form a basis for the kernel of $A$.

assumptions.assumption: Entries of the matrix $A$ belong to a field $K$ over which Gaussian elimination and pivot inversion are defined.
assumptions.breaks_when: The entries are from an arbitrary ring without division or field structure.

assumptions.assumption: The matrix $A$ represents a linear map between finite-dimensional vector spaces.
assumptions.breaks_when: The linear map acts on infinite-dimensional vector spaces where matrix block reduction is not applicable.

failure_modes.signature: Matrix $B$ has no zero columns, yielding an empty basis set for the kernel.
failure_modes.cause: $\operatorname{rank}(A) = n$, which by the rank-nullity theorem implies $\operatorname{nullity}(A) = 0$, so $\operatorname{Null}(A) = \{\mathbf{0}\}$.

failure_modes.mode: Numerical round-off error in floating-point reduction
failure_modes.signature: Zero columns in $B$ contain small non-zero residues, leading to misclassification of pivot vs. free columns.
failure_modes.cause: Floating-point cancellation and rounding during elimination obscure whether an entry is mathematically zero.
